papers.title_in_file: Quantum-inspired classical algorithm for graph problems by Gaussian boson sampling
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sections V and VI (discussion); numerical sections skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A quantum-inspired classical sampler for densest k-subgraph and maximum weight clique, compared numerically against Gaussian boson samplers.

assertions.value: The authors report numerical comparisons of ideal and lossy Gaussian boson samplers, their quantum-inspired classical sampler and a uniform sampler, and state that the advantage from Gaussian boson samplers is not significant in general.
quotes: numerically compare the performance of ideal and lossy Gaussian boson samplers, our quantum-inspired classical sampler, and the uniform sampler for ﬁnding the densest k-subgraph
show that the advantage from Gaussian boson samplers is not signiﬁcant in general
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical numerical comparison on the studied graphs; not a proof.
assertions.reader_inference: Bears on claims that GBS gives a practical advantage for graph problems.

assertions.value: The authors state that the adjacency matrix to be encoded in a Gaussian boson sampler is nonnegative, which does not necessitate quantum interference.
quotes: is nonnegative, which does not necessitate quantum interference.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author statement of the main observation behind the algorithm.

assertions.value: The authors state that it might be possible to find a better classical algorithm than theirs.
quotes: However, it might be possible to ﬁnd a better classical algorithm than our algorithm
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state the limit of their own result, Section VI (Discussions).

papers.title_in_file: A Photonic Parameter-shift Rule: Enabling Gradient Computation for Photonic Quantum Computers
papers.what_it_is: A Quandela and Quantinuum paper deriving an exact parameter-shift rule for gradients in linear optical quantum circuits.

assertions.value: The authors state they introduce a photonic parameter-shift rule that provides an exact formula for gradient computation in linear optical quantum processors, scaling linearly with the number of input photons.
quotes: providing an exact formula for gradient computation in linear optical quantum processors. Our method scales linearly with the number of input photons
assertions.certainty_reason: Derivation is in the paper body; this assertion rests on the abstract statement of the result.

assertions.value: The authors report numerical simulations in quantum chemistry and generative modeling and state that the rule showed superior optimization performance and robustness to finite-sampling noise and photon distinguishability compared to other gradient-based and gradient-free methods.
quotes: numerical simulations in quantum chemistry and generative modeling tasks, showing superior optimization performance as well as robustness to noise from finite sampling and photon distinguishability compared to other gradient-based and gradient-free methods
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation results from the authors, two applications only; vendor-authored.
assertions.reader_inference: Authors are from Quandela (hardware vendor); simulations, not hardware runs.

assertions.value: The authors state that as problem scale grows the optimization task will likely face high dimensional non-convex landscapes, and that this will necessitate going beyond l2 geometry.
quotes: will likely face high dimensional non-convex landscapes. This will necessitate going beyond l2 geometry
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state a limitation in the Discussion, Section 4.

papers.title_in_file: Hybrid Genetic Optimisation for Quantum Feature Map Design
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Conclusion; experiment sections skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A study that replaces accuracy with kernel-target alignment as the fitness in genetic design of quantum feature maps for QSVMs.

assertions.value: The authors report that, across nine binary classification problems from the UCI repository, kernel-target alignment and its approximation produce feature map circuits with comparable accuracy to previous work but with larger margins on training data (in excess of 20% larger).
quotes: A total of eight new approaches are compared to the original across nine varied binary classiﬁcation problems from the UCI machine learning repository
with larger margins on training data (in excess of 20% larger)
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on nine UCI datasets, one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the new approaches were shown to still be effective at designing accurate classifiers with fewer kernel evaluations, although at the cost of increased circuit size.
quotes: The new approaches were shown to still be eﬀective at designing accurate classiﬁers with fewer kernel evaluations, although at the cost of increased circuit size.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical; the circuit-size cost is a stated limitation of the approach.

assertions.value: The authors state there is still more work to be done in accelerating the genetic algorithm while keeping gate costs low.
quotes: There is still more work to be done in accelerating the genetic algorithm while keeping gate costs low.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state the open limit in the Conclusion, Section 4.

papers.title_in_file: NISQ-compatible approximate quantum algorithm for unconstrained and constrained discrete optimization
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Conclusion; method and results sections skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A Terra Quantum paper proposing a gradient-based quantum algorithm (QuEnc) with amplitude encoding for MaxCut and constrained binary optimization.

assertions.value: The authors report that, on unconstrained MaxCut problems with more than 1000 nodes, the hybrid approach combining their algorithm with the classical solver CPLEX realizes a better solution than CPLEX alone.
quotes: being applied to unconstrained MaxCut problems with more than 1000 nodes, the hybrid approach combining our algorithm with a classical solver called CPLEX realizes a better solution than the CPLEX alone.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result on complete weighted MaxCut graphs; one study by a vendor.

assertions.value: The authors state they tested the algorithm on MaxCut with complete weighted graphs with thousands of nodes in numerical simulations and ran the algorithm on a superconducting quantum processor.
quotes: We employ numerical simulations to test it on MaxCut problems with complete weighted graphs with thousands of nodes and run the algorithm on a superconducting quantum pro
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper states its own test setup in the Abstract and Conclusion (Section 7).

assertions.value: The authors state that QuEnc encodes the problem in probabilities that lead to a linear number of measurements in the number of classical variables.
quotes: the QuEnc encodes the problem in probabilities that lead to the linear number of measurements in the number of classical variables.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state a cost property of their own method in Section 7.

papers.title_in_file: A Hybrid Classical Quantum Computing Approach to the Satellite Mission Planning Problem
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section V Conclusions; evaluation sections skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A TUM proof-of-concept applying VQE, QAOA and warm-start QAOA to the Satellite Mission Planning Problem.

assertions.value: The authors state they demonstrate the applicability of solving the satellite mission planning problem with VQE, QAOA and W-QAOA for up to 21 locations to choose from.
quotes: we demonstrate the applicability of solving the SMPP for up to 21 locations to choose from.
assertions.certainty_reason: Proof-of-concept simulation result.

assertions.value: The authors state that instances were evaluated in a noise-free simulation with up to 21 locations and a noise-aware simulation with up to 14 locations, often leading to close-to-optimal results.
quotes: noise-free with up to 21 to-be-captured locations and a noise-aware simulation with up to 14 to-be-captured locations—often leading to (close-to) optimal results.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper states its own evaluation setup and scope, Section V.

assertions.value: The authors state that the proposed quantum approach cannot compete with the classical solutions yet.
quotes: Although the proposed quantum approach cannot compete with the classical solutions yet
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state the limit of their own approach, Section V Conclusions.

papers.title_in_file: Hybrid tree tensor networks for quantum simulation
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Section V Conclusions; method and results sections skimmed
papers.what_it_is: An IBM-led paper introducing a local-optimization algorithm for hybrid tree tensor networks, tested on the Ising model and Toric code.

assertions.value: The authors state they benchmarked their approach on the Ising model at the critical point and the Toric code Hamiltonian, and that in both cases hybrid tree tensor networks improve upon classical equivalents with equal bond dimension in the classical part.
quotes: We benchmark our approach on two paradigmatic models, namely the Ising model at the critical point and the Toric code Hamiltonian. In both cases, we successfully demonstrate that hTTNs can improve upon classical equivalents with equal bond dimension in the classical part.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation benchmarks on small systems by one group.

assertions.value: The authors state they applied the local optimization algorithm to the 8-, 16- and 4 × 4-site transverse field Ising model and the 4 × 4 and 8 × 8-site Toric code.
quotes: the 8-, 16and 4 × 4-site transverse field Ising model and the 4 × 4and 8 × 8-site Toric code
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper states its own tested scope, Section V.

assertions.value: The authors state that the VQE-like optimization scheme applied to quantum tensors may not scale to more than a few tens of qubits, due to known trainability issues of large parameterized quantum circuits.
quotes: may not scale to more than a few tens of qubits, due – for instance – to known issues about the trainability of large parameterized quantum circuits
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state a limitation in Section V Conclusions.

papers.title_in_file: Pulsar Classification: Comparing Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks and Quantum Support Vector Machines
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section V Conclusion; method and results skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study comparing 8-qubit QSVM and QCNN on binary classification of the HTRU-2 pulsar data set.

assertions.value: The authors state that simulations illustrate that both quantum methods successfully achieve effective classification of the HTRU-2 data set.
quotes: it is illustrated with simulations that both quantum methods successfully achieve effective classification of the HTRU-2 data set
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation on one data set.

assertions.value: The authors state that QCNNs outperform QSVMs in time taken to train and predict, but that with noise included for current NISQ devices, QSVMs are preferred and perform better overall on the performance metrics.
quotes: QCNNs outperform the QSVMs with respect to time taken to train and predict
QSVMs are preferred. QSVMs also perform better overall compared to QCNNs
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated and limited real-device comparison on one data set.

assertions.value: The authors state that QSVMs scale quadratically with sample size, which makes them unattractive for big-data problems.
quotes: QSVMs, however, scale quadratically with sample size, which makes them really unattractive for big-data problems.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state the limit of the method in Section V.

papers.title_in_file: A quantum-inspired classical algorithm for recommendation systems
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Section 1 Introduction (1.1 to 1.4), statements of Theorems 1 and 2; proofs not checked in detail
papers.what_it_is: Ewin Tang's dequantization of the Kerenidis-Prakash quantum recommendation system algorithm.

assertions.value: The paper states an algorithm that, given a matrix in a data structure supporting l2-norm sampling operations, outputs an l2-norm sample from a rank-k approximation in time O(poly(k) log(mn)), and that as a consequence Kerenidis and Prakash's algorithm does not give an exponential speedup over classical algorithms.
quotes: outputs an ℓ2-norm sample from a rank-k approximation of that matrix in time O(poly(k) log(mn))
does not in fact give an exponential speedup over classical algorithms.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1 (Section 4.3) with the Theorem 2 consequence for recommendations, Section 5.3.
assertions.reader_inference: Holds under the l2-norm sampling data-structure input assumption, which is the classical counterpart of the quantum state-preparation assumption.

assertions.value: The paper states that its classical recommendation system is exponentially faster than previous classical systems only under strong input assumptions.
quotes: under strong input assumptions, the classical recommendation system resulting from our algorithm produces recommendations exponentially faster than previous classical systems
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper states the scope of its own result in the Abstract.

assertions.value: The paper states that the exponents and constant factors are large, that the model assumptions are somewhat constrictive, and that it is unclear whether the algorithm performs well when the assumptions are not satisfied.
quotes: the model assumptions are somewhat constrictive. It is unclear whether the algorithm still performs well when such assumptions are not satisﬁed.
the exponents and constant factors are large
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors state limits in Section 1.4 Further Questions.
